title.narrative: Research on Strategies for Tackling Ritual Child Abuse in DRC

description.narrative: We plan to conduct a need assessment of street children stigmatised as witches in 4 most deprived boroughs in Kinshasa DRC to inform a proposed self management project which seeks to bring hope to abused children, promote children's rights and stand-up against ritual child abuse. The assesment will address the needs of these children, , those who deliver services to them and the mapping of resources providing solutions. War, instability and poverty has changed the family dynamic in the DRC. Increasingly children have been used as scapegoats when things go wrong. For example, currently some 14,000 young people accused as witches are living on the streets in DRC's Kinshasa There is little social welfare or effective laws /policies and no protection services for child in general in DRC. This research project will: - recruit and train 10 volunteers on participatory consultative research techniques to obtain the views and experiences of street children accused of withcraft; - document attitudes towards children and witchcraft in families, local organisations, churches and schools. Activities will include: workshops, group discussions and face -to-face interviews with local people The result will be a written report into work and its impact with recommendations on future action .
